questions.solution_html:
• How should a rescuer modify choking relief for an obese victim? / [CO5]
  • Ans. Perform chest thrusts instead of abdominal thrusts (due to large abdomen).
  • Place hands at the center of the chest (sternum).
  • Give quick inward thrusts until the object is expelled or victim becomes unresponsive.
  • (3 marks) for any 3 relevant points)

questions.question: Explain the AVPU scale and its role in assessing a casualty’s level of consciousness.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the A VPU scale and its role in assessing a casualty’s level of consciousness. / [CO1]
  • Ans. The A VPU scale is a simple and quick method used in first aid to assess a casualty’s level
  • of consciousness.
  • A – Alert: Patient is fully awake and responsive. (1 mark)
  • V – Verbal: Responds only to verbal stimuli. (1 mark)
  • P – Pain: Responds only to painful stimuli. (1 mark)
  • U – Unresponsive: No response to any stimulus. (1 mark)
  • Role: It helps responders determine how responsive a person is and guides immediate medical
  • action. (1 mark)

questions.question: Imagine a person is not breathing, and think they may have a spine injury. Which is more crucial, opening the airway or supporting the spine?
questions.solution_html:
• Imagine a person is not breathing, and think they may have a spine injury. Which is more crucial,
  • opening the airway or supporting the spine?
  • Ans. Airway is the priority because breathing is essential for life. (1 mark)
  • Use jaw-thrust manoeuvre to open airway without moving neck. (1 mark)
  • Maintain spinal alignment while opening airway. (1 mark)
  • If airway is blocked, it can lead to brain damage/death quickly. (1 mark)
  • Hence, a combination of airway management with spine protection is crucial. (1 mark)
  • / [CO3]
